<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Acquisition of Meridian Commodities – Strategic Concerns</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase supply, decrease demand, and increase customer choice. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the state buy a crumbling logistics network instead of investing in rural infrastructure.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study. Director Vikram needs to make the details public as soon as possible so stakeholders can understand the full implications. For instance, what happens to existing forward contracts? Will they be assigned to Meridian? Will farmers in Maharashtra have the right to choose suppliers going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can make their own procurement decisions going forward. We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is giving farmers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our receivables are going to be settled in full. If the receivables aren't paid in full, highly likely that we'll see involuntary bankruptcy.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of money and pain.

Why do you need to include the logistics purchase in this deal? May never happen. Make it easy – just deal with the working capital shortfall through securitization and through the refinancing arrangement to Meridian and get on with it.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Meridian Commodities Memorandum of Understanding:

• Commitment to Provide Commodity Supply – Meridian will keep its current sourcing operations and other supply assets and commit them to provide commodities on a regulated cost-of-service basis for 10 years.

• Renewable Sourcing Initiative – Saffron Valley Agro will commit the entire output of the Nashik facility (one of Saffron Valley's non-regulated sourcing operations) to the procurement programme on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of the Nashik facility is to be brought online by 14 August 2024. If not brought online by 14 August 2024, Saffron Valley Agro shall be assessed a ₹1.8 crore penalty.
